record.title: Shanghai prioritizes computing facilities in its green-power direct-connection pilot plan
record.summary: Shanghai’s Development and Reform Commission issued a city implementation plan for single- and multi-user direct connections between renewable generators and electricity users. The original Chinese notice prioritizes computing facilities, sets source-load matching and self-use conditions, requires grid-connected projects to pay transmission and system-operation fees, and establishes an application, evaluation and project-library process. The plan targets 500 MW of generation-side project development by 2030. A bounded official-index check did not retrieve the first selected-project library promised after the 15 Aug 2026 application deadline; project selection, data-centre economics and operating outcomes remain unknown.
organizations: Shanghai Municipal Development and Reform Commission

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Shanghai DRC’s notice 沪发改能源〔2026〕140号 prioritizes computing facilities for direct green-power projects and defines application, source/load, grid-fee and project-management rules.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: This review did not retrieve a selected-project library or evidence of a compute facility’s selection, delivered energy cost or operation.

evidence_gaps.description: Shanghai DRC stated it would publish selected projects after first-batch review; this bounded check did not retrieve the project library.
No project-level delivered cost or metered compute-facility operation was inspected.

brief.importance_rationale: If implemented, direct renewable supply and its source-load, storage, grid-fee and settlement conditions could change procurement and siting choices for Shanghai compute projects. The local scope and absence of selected-project, delivered-cost or operating evidence constrain the consequence assessment.
limitations: The first-batch selected-project library was not retrieved in the bounded Shanghai DRC index/search check after the stated 15 Aug 2026 submission deadline. Do not infer non-publication or no compute selection.
No project-specific contract tariff, transmission/system charges, storage/balancing costs, metered load, renewable matching or operational performance was inspected.
The 2030 figure is a policy target, not realized generation or direct-supply capacity.
organizations: Shanghai Municipal Development and Reform Commission
brief.summary: Shanghai’s Development and Reform Commission issued a city implementation plan for single- and multi-user direct connections between renewable generators and electricity users. The original Chinese notice prioritizes computing facilities, sets source-load matching and self-use conditions, requires grid-connected projects to pay transmission and system-operation fees, and establishes an application, evaluation and project-library process. The plan targets 500 MW of generation-side project development by 2030. A bounded official-index check did not retrieve the first selected-project library promised after the 15 Aug 2026 application deadline; project selection, data-centre economics and operating outcomes remain unknown.

technical.claimed_result: Shanghai states it will prioritize computing facilities for direct green-power projects and target 500,000 kW generation-side development by 2030.
technical.compute_or_cost: Grid-connected projects must fairly bear transmission and system-operation charges under national rules. No data-centre tariff, storage cost, delivered cost or savings were measured.
technical.demonstrated_result: The original-language DRC notice establishes the policy text, compute priority, application and project management rules, and stated 2030 generation-side target; no project selection or actual energy outcome is established.
technical.implementation_status: Notice 沪发改能源〔2026〕140号 issued 17 Jul and published 20 Jul 2026. The notice requested first-batch submissions by 15 Aug and said selected projects would be made public after evaluation; no selected-project library was retrieved in this bounded check.
technical.mechanism: Shanghai screens single-user and multi-user renewable direct-supply projects, prioritizes compute facilities, defines grid-connected/off-grid cases, minimum self-use shares, system-friendly balancing and fee obligations, and ties construction/operation to an approved project library.
technical.novelty: A Shanghai implementation route explicitly prioritizing compute loads for direct renewable supply with project-level grid, balancing and tracing rules.
technical.regime: Shanghai municipal green-power direct-connection pilot; projects can be single-user or multi-user, grid-connected or off-grid, subject to project screening and source/load conditions.
technical.reproducibility: The notice and its policy index are accessible via the Shanghai DRC site; selected-project library status and project outcomes require a separate search.
technical.strongest_baseline: The notice implements national green-power direct-connection guidance locally; it distinguishes the policy pathway from ordinary grid supply but provides no matched tariff or operating baseline.

brief.title: Shanghai prioritizes computing facilities in its green-power direct-connection pilot plan
brief.why_it_matters: The plan gives compute facilities explicit priority in a local procurement/infrastructure pathway while retaining balancing, grid-fee and performance conditions. It creates a route worth tracking for Shanghai compute sourcing, but does not show cheaper or greener electricity at any facility.
